subject: Migration prioritization: rollout asks and exception gate
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Migration prioritization: quick ask + proposed pacing

Hi Sarah and team,

Thanks again for walking through the migration changes this morning. I wanted to capture a short, concrete ask so our cross-functional team can unblock scheduling and exceptions if needed.

Two items from our side:
1) Prioritization window: Can you confirm which of your endpoints will need the new streaming model by July 15 vs. those that can be phased in Sept? We need this split to size Dedicated capacity.
2) Runbook exceptions: For the two critical webhooks you mentioned (billing-notify and order-fulfill), we think a temporary exception/compat-lane is safer than immediate cutover. Would a 30-day exception working + opt-in be acceptable?

Attached is a first-pass migration-plan-v1.pdf and a short runbook-diff.txt that highlights the behavioral changes we saw during internal tests.

Next steps I propose: internal triage tomorrow at 10am PT (Marissa/Product + Irene/Eng + Dylan/Support) then a follow-up sync with you on Friday to lock dates. If this looks OK, Marissa will capture the exception gate and draft the comms.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

Attachments: migration-plan-v1.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB), runbook-diff.txt (text, 8KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

+1 on the proposed cadence. A few internal notes before we loop Acme back in:

- Irene: we need an explicit list of behavioral diffs we can publish in the customer-facing doc. The runbook-diff is great but terse — can you expand the top 3 user-impact items?
- Dylan: CS needs a fallback script for the billing-notify webhook so support can toggle back if customers see double-notify. Can you draft that?
- Ben: can you flag any capacity constraints if we have a July 15 partial migration for a 50% traffic shift?

Irene/Ben/Dylan — please reply inline with ETA. Priyom, I’ll take point on the exception gate language and the comms template. I’ll draft the customer-facing note once we have Irene’s user-impact bullets.

Marissa
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Marissa — capturing the top three user-impact items below (ETA: sending doc update by EOD):

1) Response ordering: under the new model some batched requests may return tokens earlier; most customers are unaffected, but systems doing incremental diffs may need to rehydrate and reconcile.
2) Socket keep-alives: clients with 60s idle timeout may see streaming disconnects unless they continue to read the stream; we provide a small client helper in SDK v0.8 to reattach streams.
3) Embedding schema: the float precision changed slightly (quantization profile); customers persisting exact vectors will need a short reindex job.

On the two webhooks: I agree with the exception lane for billing-notify and order-fulfill. Proposed exception approach:
- 30-day opt-in: customers stay on legacy model for up to 30 days post-cutover, traffic pinned server-side.
- Automatic telemetry: flag any mismatch events for our QA team.

I’ll push a short customer-impact section into the migration plan (drive link included). If Acme needs a longer exception, we’ll surface to leadership.

— Irene
Director, Serving Platform

- We can split endpoints: billing-notify + order-fulfill -> July 15 exception lane; other less-critical flows go Sept 1. We’ll provide a final list by Thursday EOD.
- 30-day opt-in sounds fine. Our security/compliance team asked for the exception to be documented in the contract amendment; I’ve looped legal and will send us a DocuSign link if that’s required.

Appreciate the clear plan — Sarah
